name: NHX-01 — Whispers in the Static
description: A signal image was recovered from the fictional HEX-SHADOW incident. Inspect the image and recover a flag and the E01 evidence fragment. Keep each fragment for NoctiCore.
hints: An image can contain information that is not visible.
Inspect both metadata and embedded file structures.

name: NHX-02 — Cipher at Dusk
description: HEX-SHADOW encoded a dispatch in multiple layers. Identify the transformations and reverse them in order. Recover the flag and E02. The story follows NHX-01; this stage is independently accessible.
hints: Encoding and encryption are not the same thing.
The outer layer uses a common Base64 representation.

name: NHX-03 — Mirror Account
description: Investigate the fictional employee portal at /labs/nhx03/. Training credentials: tester / noctihex123. Inspect how the portal identifies profile records. Recover the flag and E03. Only test this local challenge.
hints: Observe the profile identifier in your browser address.
Authentication and object-level authorization are separate checks.

name: NHX-04 — Packet After Midnight
description: A synthetic capture contains several fictional conversations. Identify the HEX-SHADOW communication, inspect its stream, and recover the flag and E04. No live traffic capture is needed.
hints: Start with Statistics and Conversations instead of inspecting every packet manually.
Look for unusual HTTP paths and identify the suspicious host.

name: NHX-05 — Misplaced Trust
description: Connect to the local fictional backup server: ssh analyst@127.0.0.1 -p 2225. Training password: nocti2026. Inspect your permissions and the custom backup utility. Recover the protected flag and E05 using its intended path-validation flaw. Stay inside this challenge container.
hints: Check the commands the analyst user is permitted to execute.
Investigate how the backup utility decides whether a file path is allowed.

name: NHX-06 — NoctiCore
description: Analyze the Linux x86-64 executable in Linux or WSL. Reconstruct its verification algorithm and combine E01 through E05 in stage order, separated by |. Run the executable with the evidence chain to recover the final flag. Preserve exact case; do not add spaces.
hints: The previous stages contain more than individual flags.
Five fragments form one chain. Their order matters.
The executable calculates a 32-bit verification value from its input.
